messages.content: Race update: packet pickup is Friday 4 to 7 p.m., and they think the Sunday course closure will finish by 1. The race-area lodge now only shows double-bed rooms and still will not confirm a refrigerator. Can we make the call before that cancellable suite rate disappears?

Yes. I would move away from the lodge. It is close to the race, but the room setup is now weaker: double beds only, refrigerator still unverified, and no clear recovery amenities. The downtown suite is the practical pick: queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, hot tub, fitness room. Caveats are the parking fee and a 25-minute race-morning drive.
That is where my head is too. I do not want maybe-fridge plus double beds after a trail race.

Then I’d book the downtown suite on the refundable rate. It keeps the Friday arrival easy enough for packet pickup and gives you a better post-race reset. I’ll note the drive: plan to leave the hotel earlier than feels necessary Sunday morning, especially if parking near the start backs up.
What about getting there? Is flying into Atlanta with a rental still better than driving the whole thing?

For this version of the weekend, yes. Driving Tampa-Chattanooga gives control, but the return is the rough part after the race. TPA-ATL plus a rental keeps the long highway stretch shorter, and the Sunday Atlanta flights work if you leave Chattanooga shortly after lunch.
Okay. Book the suite, and use the fly-and-rent plan. Friday should leave enough room for packet pickup. Sunday give us lunch, the drive to Atlanta, and no sprint through the airport.

Best fit: Friday TPA-ATL arriving 10:38 a.m., rental pickup around 11, Chattanooga around 1:30 to 2 depending on the stop. Sunday: leave Chattanooga about 1:15, return the car at ATL by 3:45, and take the 5:35 p.m. ATL-TPA.
That works. Adjacent seats if possible; I can take the window. Keep the hotel cancellable.

Booked. Downtown queen studio suite, refundable until 48 hours before arrival, with coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, hot tub, and fitness room confirmed; parking fee added to the notes. Flights are TPA-ATL Friday morning and ATL-TPA Sunday at 5:35 p.m.; seats 16A and 16B are selected. Rental is set from ATL Friday to Sunday. Main caveat left: the Sunday plan depends on leaving Chattanooga soon after lunch.

messages.content: New one: a Denver-area children's hospital wants me for a pediatric neurodevelopment course in mid-January. Teaching would be Thursday and Friday, and they are still deciding about Saturday morning consults. I can leave Tampa after my Wednesday morning class. Can you compare the practical options, not just the cheapest ones?
Absolutely. Before I rank it, two timing checks: what is the earliest you can realistically be at TPA on Wednesday, and how protected does Sunday need to be before your Monday remote block?
I can be at the airport around noon if I leave class cleanly. Monday remote teaching starts at 9 a.m., so I do not want a late Sunday night arrival or a fragile Saturday plan if the consults happen.

Good. I’d frame this around winter reliability. Wednesday flight options: 1) nonstop TPA-DEN leaving a little after 2 p.m., arriving before dinner, higher fare but lowest disruption risk; 2) one-stop through Dallas leaving around 12:40, arriving around 5:45, cheaper but connection-sensitive; 3) late one-stop routings through northern hubs, cheapest in spots but not attractive for a Thursday teaching start.
Please keep the hotel caveats plain too. The hospital-adjacent one sounds convenient, but I do not want the fridge issue buried.

Plain version: the hospital-adjacent hotel wins on commute and has solid recent feedback, around 4.2/5 in current guest ratings. It can show queen rooms and basic in-room coffee, but refrigerator availability is by request, not guaranteed, and it does not have a hot tub. The suite hotel about 15 minutes away is better rated, around 4.6/5, and confirms queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, hot tub, and fitness room. Trade-off: parking fee and possible snow-related drive time.
If the Saturday consults happen, what does the return day look like?

Saturday return is possible but tight. If consults end by noon, you would need bags already handled, leave the hospital around 12:30, and get to DEN around 2 to 2:15 in decent road conditions. A late-afternoon nonstop works on paper. If consults run long, or if snow slows the drive, the cushion gets thin quickly.
And Sunday?

Sunday is calmer. There are afternoon departures that get you back to Tampa early evening instead of late night. It adds one hotel night, but it protects the Saturday consult block and gives you a real buffer before Monday morning.
I can justify the extra night if Saturday is really part of the work. What does the hospital need to confirm before I commit?

They need to confirm: whether Saturday consults are happening; the hard end time, ideally noon; whether they can receive and securely store your demo materials before you arrive; Thursday and Friday room access time; AV, treatment table, floor mats, and any pediatric equipment they expect you to use; where you enter and park; and whether travel reimbursement covers Saturday work, the extra hotel night, parking, and ground transport.
Is the Dallas connection cheap enough to take seriously, or is that asking for trouble in January?

It is worth seeing, but I would not pick a short connection. The Dallas option I see is roughly $130 to $170 less than the nonstop, with about a 70-minute connection. That is not terrible, but a delay leaving Tampa could put your Wednesday evening at risk. For a Thursday morning teaching start, the nonstop buys useful insurance.
Rank the whole package for me.

Most practical: Wednesday nonstop, suite hotel, Sunday afternoon return. It costs more, but it has the cleanest flight risk, the clearest room setup, and the best Monday recovery. Middle path: Wednesday nonstop, hospital-adjacent hotel, Sunday return. Commute is easier, but refrigerator remains a caveat and there is no hot tub. Cheapest but fragile: Dallas connection, hospital-adjacent hotel, Saturday late return. I would only use that if the hospital drops Saturday and confirms the room details tightly.
Could the hospital-adjacent hotel still make sense if they guarantee the refrigerator?

Yes. If they put the refrigerator confirmation in writing with the reservation, the adjacent hotel becomes a very reasonable bad-weather choice because the commute is simpler. It still lacks the hot tub, so the suite remains better for recovery, but the adjacent hotel could win if snow is forecast or if the course day starts very early.
Good. Draft the short list of questions for the hospital. Add that I need the Saturday decision next week because I cannot keep the return open indefinitely.

Send them this: Please confirm by next week whether Saturday consults are included and, if so, the guaranteed end time. Can you receive and store my demo materials two days before arrival? What room access time, AV, mats, tables, and pediatric equipment will be available Thursday and Friday? Which entrance and parking area should I use in winter weather? If I stay through Sunday to support Saturday consults, will the added hotel night, parking, and ground transport be reimbursed? Also, if you want me at the hospital-adjacent hotel, please confirm a queen room with coffee maker and a guaranteed refrigerator in writing. I would hold off booking until those answers come back.

messages.content: Denver update: the host confirmed Saturday consults, hard stop by noon, and they can receive my demo materials two days before I arrive. Let's book this.

Great, that removes the biggest open issue. The decision now is mostly about risk versus cost: Wednesday nonstop versus the cheaper Dallas connection, and Saturday late return versus Sunday afternoon.
I do not want the Saturday return. If the roads are slow or consults run even a little over, I will be annoyed all day. Use Sunday afternoon unless it is wildly expensive.

Sunday afternoon is reasonable. The nonstop DEN-TPA at 1:35 p.m. gets into Tampa around 6:55 p.m. It adds the extra hotel night, but it gives you a calm Saturday and a usable Sunday evening before Monday teaching.
Good. What is the fare difference on the outbound?

Wednesday nonstop TPA-DEN leaves at 2:05 p.m. and arrives 4:22 p.m.; fare is about $418. The Dallas one-stop leaves 12:40 p.m., arrives 5:45 p.m., and is about $289, but the connection is only 70 minutes. For January and a Thursday course start, the nonstop is the safer pattern.
Use the nonstop. I need that evening to land, eat, and not be troubleshooting.

For hotel, the adjacent property can guarantee queen and coffee maker now, but still will not guarantee the refrigerator, and there is no hot tub. The suite hotel confirms queen studio, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, hot tub, and fitness room. Caveats: $18 nightly parking and the hospital drive may be longer than 15 minutes if snow hits.
Book the suite. The refrigerator uncertainty at the close hotel is not worth it.

I can book the refundable queen studio Wednesday through Sunday. Do you also want a rental? The suite location is workable by rideshare, but for Saturday materials and winter timing, a small SUV would give more control.
Yes, add a rental that can handle snow without being huge. Cancellable if possible.

Best fit is a midsize SUV with AWD requested, pickup at DEN Wednesday around 4:45 p.m. and return Sunday around 11:30 a.m. It is cancellable. Caveat: the agency will note AWD, but they do not absolutely guarantee it until the counter assigns the vehicle.
That caveat is fine. Window seat if the seat map is open.

Booked. Flights: Wednesday TPA-DEN nonstop 2:05-4:22, seat 12A; Sunday DEN-TPA nonstop 1:35-6:55, seat 18A. Hotel: refundable queen studio suite Wednesday-Sunday with coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, hot tub, and fitness room; parking fee noted. Rental: cancellable midsize SUV with AWD requested, with the AWD assignment caveat noted. Host logistics are also noted: demo materials accepted two days before arrival and Saturday consults ending by noon.
